tasks.title: Default integer
tasks.statement:
Declare n = 2147483647 (that is i32::MAX) and print n. Then print the value of the constant i32::MIN. Two lines.

Expected output:
2147483647
-2147483648
tasks.hint: i32::MIN is a type constant; it prints like an ordinary number.

tasks.title: Bounds of u8 and i8
tasks.statement:
Print u8::MIN, u8::MAX, i8::MIN, i8::MAX separated by spaces: «0 255 -128 127».

Expected output:
0 255 -128 127

tasks.title: A big number
tasks.statement:
Declare big: i64 = 5_000_000_000 and print big * 2 («10000000000»). With the type i32 such a number would not fit.

Expected output:
10000000000
tasks.hint: Put an explicit type i64 after the colon.

tasks.title: Type sizes
tasks.statement:
Print the sizes in bytes of the types u8, i32, f64, char, bool, one per line: 1, 4, 8, 4, 1. The function is std::mem::size_of::<T>().

Expected output:
1
4
8
4
1
tasks.hint: The type goes in angle brackets: size_of::<u8>().

tasks.title: Integer division and remainder
tasks.statement:
Print three lines: 17 / 5, 17 % 5 and 17.0 / 5.0. Expected: «3», «2» and «3.4».

Expected output:
3
2
3.4
tasks.hint: Integers give an integer result, floats give a fractional one.

tasks.title: Remainder with a negative number
tasks.statement:
Print -7 / 2, -7 % 2 and (-7_i32).rem_euclid(2), one per line: «-3», «-1», «1». In Rust the remainder takes the sign of the dividend, while rem_euclid is always non-negative.

Expected output:
-3
-1
1
tasks.hint: In Python -7 // 2 = -4, but in Rust integer division truncates toward zero.

tasks.title: Powers
tasks.statement:
Print 2^10 (using the pow method for an integer) and 1.5^3 (using the powi method for a float): «1024» and «3.375».

Expected output:
1024
3.375

tasks.title: checked_add
tasks.statement:
Print the results of 250_u8.checked_add(5) and 250_u8.checked_add(10), one per line. The method returns an Option: «Some(255)» and «None». Use {:?} to print an Option.

Expected output:
Some(255)
None
tasks.hint: println!("{:?}", …) is debug output.

tasks.title: Wrapping around
tasks.statement:
Print 250_u8.wrapping_add(10) («4»), 250_u8.saturating_add(10) («255») and 5_u8.wrapping_sub(10) («251») — three lines.

Expected output:
4
255
251
tasks.hint: wrapping goes around the circle, saturating stops at the boundary.

tasks.title: overflowing_add
tasks.statement:
Print 200_u8.overflowing_add(100) and 20_u8.overflowing_add(100). The result is a pair: «(44, true)» and «(120, false)». Use {:?} for the pair.

Expected output:
(44, true)
(120, false)
tasks.hint: A pair (result, whether_overflow_happened).

tasks.title: Fix it: the constant doesn't fit
tasks.statement:
The program does not compile: the number 300 does not fit in u8. Change the type to a suitable one (u16) so that it prints «300».

Expected output:
300
tasks.hint: u8 holds up to 255; u16 holds up to 65535.

tasks.title: Number bases
tasks.statement:
Print the number 255 as «ff» (format {:x}), as «11111111» (format {:b}) and as «377» (format {:o}) — three lines.

Expected output:
ff
11111111
377
tasks.hint: {:x} is hexadecimal, {:b} is binary, {:o} is octal notation.

tasks.title: Floating-point arithmetic
tasks.statement:
Print two lines: 10.0 / 4.0 and 10.0 % 4.0 — «2.5» and «2».

Expected output:
2.5
2
tasks.hint: The remainder is defined for floats too.

tasks.title: Float inexactness
tasks.statement:
Print 0.1 + 0.2 (it will be «0.30000000000000004»), then the result of the comparison 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 («false»), then a comparison with a tolerance: ((0.1 + 0.2) - 0.3).abs() < 1e-9 («true»).

Expected output:
0.30000000000000004
false
true
tasks.hint: Floats are compared with a tolerance, not with ==.

tasks.title: Rounding
tasks.statement:
x = 2.5. Print x.floor(), x.ceil(), x.round(), x.trunc(), one per line: «2», «3», «3», «2» (the results are floats, printed without .0 when output with {}).

Expected output:
2
3
3
2
tasks.hint: floor rounds down, ceil rounds up, round goes to the nearest (0.5 goes away from zero), trunc drops the fraction.

tasks.title: Hypotenuse
tasks.statement:
The legs are 3.0 and 4.0. Print the length of the hypotenuse using sqrt: «5».

Expected output:
5
tasks.hint: (a * a + b * b).sqrt() — sqrt is a method of a float.

tasks.title: inf and NaN
tasks.statement:
Print 1.0 / 0.0, -1.0 / 0.0 and 0.0 / 0.0 (three lines: «inf», «-inf», «NaN»), and then (0.0_f64 / 0.0).is_nan() («true»).

Expected output:
inf
-inf
NaN
true
tasks.hint: The type f64 is given so that the compiler understands the is_nan method.

tasks.title: Casts with as
tasks.statement:
Print one per line: 3.99_f64 as i32 («3»), 300_i32 as u8 («44»), -1_i32 as u32 («4294967295»), 65_u8 as char («A»).

Expected output:
3
44
4294967295
A
tasks.hint: as cuts off bits and the fractional part.

tasks.title: Fix it: mixed types
tasks.statement:
You cannot add an i32 and an f64 without a conversion. Fix the program so that it prints «7.5».

Expected output:
7.5
tasks.hint: a as f64 + b

tasks.title: Lossless From
tasks.statement:
Declare a: u8 = 200 and b: i64 = 5_000_000_000. Print the sum i64::from(a) + b: «5000000200».

Expected output:
5000000200
tasks.hint: i64::from(a) safely widens u8 to i64.

tasks.title: try_from
tasks.statement:
Print u8::try_from(200_i32).is_ok() and u8::try_from(300_i32).is_ok() — «true» and «false».

Expected output:
true
false
tasks.hint: try_from returns a Result; .is_ok() tells whether it worked.

tasks.title: Parsing a number from text
tasks.statement:
Parse the strings «41» and «3.5» into i32 and f64 with the parse method and unwrap. Print the sum n + 1 and the product x * 2.0: «42» and «7».

Expected output:
42
7
tasks.hint: let n: i32 = "41".parse().unwrap(); — the type comes from the annotation.

tasks.title: parse with an error
tasks.statement:
For the strings «12», «abc» and «-5», print whether they could be turned into an i32: «true», «false», «true» (the method parse::<i32>().is_ok()).

Expected output:
true
false
true
tasks.hint: The type can be given with the turbofish: parse::<i32>().

tasks.title: Logic
tasks.statement:
Let a = true, b = false. Print a && b, a || b, !a, a && !b, one per line: «false», «true», «false», «true».

Expected output:
false
true
false
true
tasks.hint: && is "and", || is "or", ! is "not".

tasks.title: Comparisons
tasks.statement:
x = 15. Print the results of: x > 10, x == 15, x != 15, x >= 20, and the range check x >= 10 && x <= 20 — five lines: true, true, false, false, true.

Expected output:
true
true
false
false
true
tasks.hint: The result of a comparison is a bool, so you can print it directly.

tasks.title: Fix it: the condition is not a bool
tasks.statement:
The if has a number in it, which is an error. Fix the condition so that it prints «non-zero» for n = 5.

Expected output:
```
non-zero
```
tasks.hint: The condition is an explicit comparison n != 0.

tasks.title: Characters
tasks.statement:
c = `'ж'`. Print the character itself, then its code via as u32 («1078»), then c.is_alphabetic() («true»), and '7'.is_numeric() («true») — one per line.

Expected output:
```
ж
1078
true
true
```
tasks.hint: `'ж'` as u32 is the character's Unicode code.

tasks.title: Character case
tasks.statement:
For 'q' print c.to_ascii_uppercase() («Q»), for `'I'` print c.to_lowercase().next().unwrap() («i») and for the digit character '8' print '8'.to_digit(10).unwrap() + 1 («9») — three lines.

Expected output:
```
Q
i
9
```
tasks.hint: to_lowercase returns an iterator, so we take the first character with next().unwrap().

tasks.title: Shifting along the alphabet
tasks.statement:
Take 'a' and print the character that follows it in the table (via as u8 + 1 as char): «b». Then get 'z' from 'a' + 25 the same way: «z».

Expected output:
b
z
tasks.hint: (c as u8 + 1) as char

tasks.title: Final: summary of types
tasks.statement:
Declare n: i32 = -17, x: f64 = 2.5, ok: bool = true, c: char = `'I'`. Print one line with spaces in the format «n=-17 x=2.5 ok=true c=I», then on a separate line n.abs() as f64 * x («42.5»).

Expected output:
```
n=-17 x=2.5 ok=true c=I
42.5
```
tasks.hint: First cast n.abs() to f64 with as, then multiply by x.
